roofs_refused.why: THE ONE LODGING THE SOURCES ATTACH TO THIS CONGREGATION IS SOMEWHERE ELSE. The record's `occupants` note has Rev. Jeremiah Porter arriving in May 1833 and lodging 'in the unfinished loft of Peck's store'. A congregation is not a household, and the minister's bed is in another building.

THE BEST-SPECIFIED SMALL BUILDING IN THE TOWN, AND IT IS A CHURCH THROUGHOUT. The page behind this record gives two dimensions, a cost, a builder, a lumber price, an exterior and interior finish and a seating description, and describes no residence and no room set apart as one. It names Fr. St. Cyr pastor across the whole scene window and says nothing about where he slept. Naming this his dwelling would be a reconstruction bounded by nothing, in the one record that could least afford it.

TWO USES, NEITHER OF THEM A BED. The record carries the First Baptist Church Society and Grenville T. Sproat's English and Classical School for Boys in the upper storey — a meeting room and a day school. Nothing states a dwelling, and the building's owner is housed elsewhere in the layer.

CONFINEMENT IS NOT RESIDENCE. The record attests a jail of logs at the north-west corner of the court-house square and nothing else about it; no gaoler's quarters are attested, and the same record records that the county conducted its business in rented rooms. A prisoner is not a household and this project does not hold that anybody was in it on the scene date.

A ROOM THE TOWN MET IN. Andreas puts 'Billy Caldwell's log council-house' among the places services were held, beside Ingersoll's tavern and Watkins's school-house; that is a use, and the man whose it was is housed elsewhere in the layer. The record's own note says the sources describe nothing of what happened inside it.

A PURPOSE-BUILT SCHOOLHOUSE, AND THE 1835 USE IS THE TEACHING. Andreas has John Watkins teaching what had become a public school on the North Side on the river bank just east of Clark Street; the attestation is of a school in session, not of anybody living in it. Its own record carries no `occupants` block at all.

THE LEAST SETTLED RECORD IN ITS PARCEL. Two near-primary witnesses give it a double use — worship and school — and disagree about which bank of the river it stood on; its own research_note says to treat the position as a placeholder. Nothing states a dwelling, and a household seated on a building whose river bank is unresolved would be seated on a guess twice over.

what_the_book_ordered_before_the_adjudic.note: The apportionment's own figures on 2026-09-24, weighted on the nine roofs of the `institutional_public` matrix row. Kept here so the re-cut can be read as a re-cut rather than as the number always having been two.
